agents.name: Rex
agents.note:
US-503 DONE (Sprint 69 / V0.29.24, 3/10). The idle-home card clock reads 12-hour AM/PM: mod-12 with the 12 restored for midnight/noon, bare hour ('2:05 PM', never '02:05 PM'), zero-padded minute, no seconds. Purely a format change -- no data source, no state file, no emitter, and the Date is still the caller's. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: I moved fmtClock (and its two() helper) OUT of the browser-only `if (typeof document !== 'undefined')` block and up into the pure/exported section. Not a preference -- under 'use strict' an ES6 function declaration inside a block is BLOCK-SCOPED, so fmtClock was structurally unreachable from the api export literal and from every test, and hoisting does not rescue it. It was always pure (it formats the Date it is handed, it never reads one), so that block's 'the pure view logic stays clock-free, so these live in the DOM layer' comment was true of fmtDate but never of fmtClock. fmtDate + IDLE_DAYS/IDLE_MONTHS stayed put (out of scope). carousel.js now holds exactly ONE clock formatter and the DOM block CALLS it rather than owning one -- with a comment there saying so, to stop a future edit re-declaring a local. 10 tests, all 10 RED first, and the DOM one went red on the REAL rendered value '22:50' -- the actual bug, not a proxy for it. 3 mutations proved: bare `% 12` (no `|| 12`) -> midnight + noon + sweep fail; meridiem boundary `h <= 12` -> noon reads AM, caught by 2; and the load-bearing one -- RE-SHADOWING the DOM block with the old 24-hour formatter leaves ALL NINE fmtClock unit tests green and is caught ONLY by the end-to-end DOM test. That is precisely why the story has one: same two-correct-halves-never-connected shape as US-494/US-499/US-502, and this sprint has now hit that shape twice in three stories. Needed a dedicated probe (tests/ui/idle_clock_probe.js) because carousel_probe.js JSON-decodes its args and JSON has no Date -- it would pass a Number and fmtClock would read NaN; the probe builds the Date from local calendar COMPONENTS, so the fixture is the clock FACE not an instant and the assertions hold in any timezone. Green in-loop: tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 580 passed exit 0, the 10 new ones verified RUN not skipped (node present); ruff clean. Full pytest + mypy not run in-loop per TD-059, but this touches ONE JS function and zero Python source -- the blast radius is the UI suite, which ran whole. FLAG FOR THE ON-PI DRILL (layout, not logic): .idle-header is a flex row (wordmark + clock + date, gap 8px) on the 480px design stage and the clock string grew ~3 glyphs ('22:05' -> '10:05 PM'). I deliberately did NOT pre-tighten dashboard.css: the render harness resolves CSS but does no text metrics, so any change would have been a guess at a panel I cannot see. If the header crowds on the real 480x320, it is a one-line CSS follow-up. OWED: the on-Pi read of the clock at a known time. Next up is US-504 (battery-health truthfulness, L) -- NOTE its AC1 says it wires the BATTERY portion of the consolidated Health card from US-507 and that US-507 should land FIRST, but US-507 is NOT in this sprint's story list; PM may need to rule on that sequencing. Its writer-fix sub-story (battery_health_log vcell/soc NULL on all 28 rows) is independent of that and can go first regardless.

PRIOR (US-502, same sprint): the System-Status power tile + header bolt now read the real AC/battery source. The tile read PowerMonitor.readPowerStatus(), whose reader is NEVER configured in the orchestrator -> source permanently 'unknown' -> 'unavailable' tile + gray bolt, while the real GPIO6 fact already flowed to power_log via the B1 _PowerSourceUiBridge. _gatherPowerSource now reads PowerSourceProvider direct; PowerMonitor is REMOVED from that path (a second acquisition path could disagree with GPIO6 = the SSOT violation the design gate forbids). Only contract change: a new PowerSourceProvider.isAvailable property, because the shutdown path's safe direction is a LIE on a display -- an unreadable PLD deliberately answers isExternalPowerPresent()==True (never self-brick on a dead signal), and taking that at face value paints a confident lit-green 'external' off a DEAD GPIO. The provider exposes the FACT; each consumer keeps its own uncertainty policy (sequencer=treat-as-present, UI=unknown). Second trap caught: the provider is built in _startHardwareManager but the emitters are built EARLIER in _initializeAllComponents, so a reference captured at emitter-init would be None for the life of the process -- read is lazy, per emit. 17 tests, 5 mutations caught. FLAG: card_state_emitter.py is a base-module touch -- prioritise full-suite regression + mypy at integration.

PRIOR (US-501, same sprint): dashboard header version chip wired to .deploy-version via a __DEPLOY_VERSION__ placeholder substituted in states_http_server._injectHtml, on the same seam as __SPLASH_TOKEN__ / __DISPLAY_AUTODIM__ / __DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__. Read PER REQUEST, not cached at construction: deploy-pi.sh restarts eclipse-states-http (line 1939) but stamps .deploy-version LAST (line 1955), deliberately per US-354, so a start-time cache renders the PREVIOUS deploy's version on every deploy -- green tests, correct-looking code, and the exact stale literal the story deletes. Honest degrade: readDeployVersion returns None (never a guess) for no-path / absent / unreadable / malformed / missing / blank / non-string, and the chip falls back to the same 'V?.?.?' sentinel the splash uses. NO deploy or unit-file change needed. 18 tests. CAVEAT for Iris: a file:// preview shows raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ in the chip -- the quoted-placeholder trick does not work on HTML text content; deliberate, dev-only.
